nodes.name: assign
nodes.documentation:
Resolves step decisions and function membership for one intent layer.

# Errors
Returns an error for a step with an unknown cluster, or for a node whose steps
carry different clusters.

nodes.name: digests
nodes.documentation:
Computes every digest of one artifact from its layers.

# Errors
Returns an error when a layer cannot have a canonical form.

nodes.name: fact_layer
nodes.signature:
pub fn fact_layer(
    graph: &ArtifactGraph,
    binding: FactBinding,
    keys: &BTreeSet<&str>,
) -> Result<FactLayer, DeriveError>
nodes.documentation:
Projects the graph nodes with the given keys and the edges between them.

Nodes sort by key. Edges sort by source, target, and relation name, without duplicates.

# Errors
Returns an error for a graph value that the fact schema cannot hold.

nodes.name: view
nodes.signature:
pub fn view(
    facts: &FactLayer,
    intent: &IntentLayer,
    assignment: &AssignmentLayer,
    parent: Option<&ViewLayer>,
) -> ViewLayer
nodes.documentation:
Derives the view layer.

A retained cluster keeps its parent color. A new cluster takes the lowest
palette slot that no retained cluster uses and that no cluster removed in this
generation used. When those slots run out, it takes the lowest slot that no
retained cluster uses.

nodes.name: import_flow
nodes.signature:
pub fn import_flow(
    directory: &Path,
    request: ImportRequest<'_>,
) -> Result<ImportOutcome, FlowError>
nodes.documentation:
Freezes one agent output as the next generation of one flow.

A dry run takes no store lock and returns the generation that a freeze
would write.

# Errors
Returns `Rejected` with every issue when the output is invalid; nothing is
written then. Returns other errors for store or graph failures.

nodes.name: parse_output
nodes.documentation: Parses the agent output. A `no_flow` answer comes back as a finished outcome.

nodes.name: read_current
nodes.signature:
pub fn read_current(
    directory: &Path,
    flow_id: &FlowId,
) -> Result<Option<StoredGeneration>, LineageError>
nodes.documentation:
Reads the current generation of one flow, or `None` when the flow has no lineage.

A pointer that is not a regular file counts as no lineage.

# Errors
Returns an error for a link, an unreadable file, an invalid document, a
generation of another flow, or a pointer that names another generation.

nodes.name: write_current
nodes.signature: pub fn write_current(directory: &Path, artifact: &FlowArtifact) -> Result<String, LineageError>
nodes.documentation:
Writes one generation and moves the current pointer to it.

The generation file is written first, so a reader never sees a pointer to a
missing file. An identical existing generation file is kept. An entry that
is not a regular file counts as missing.

# Errors
Returns an error for a link, a file failure, or a different file at the same path.

nodes.documentation:
Canonicalizes and checks one agent flow against the graph and the prior version.

Returns the checked flow only when no error issue exists. Warnings (for
example `text_trimmed`) come back in both cases.

nodes.name: read_graph
nodes.signature: pub fn read_graph(directory: &Path, file: &str) -> io::Result<(ArtifactGraph, String)>
nodes.documentation:
Reads one graph artifact of the store and returns its graph and byte digest.

# Errors
Returns an error for an invalid name, a link, an unreadable file, or an invalid artifact.

nodes.name: write_bytes
nodes.documentation: Replaces one store file atomically. The file and its folder must not be symbolic links.

intent.behavior: How Tekdek turns a coding agent's flow output into a frozen, clustered flow: the `tekdek flow import` command parses the output and checks it against the graph, assigns clusters and derives the facts, view, and digests, and writes the generation and the current pointer.
intent.boundaries: Starts at the binary entry for `tekdek flow import` with a new flow name and follows the success path of an initial generation to the pointer write. The returns to import_flow between its calls are not shown. The step ledgers name the no_flow answer, rejected outputs, the unchanged (`kept`) result, and the revision rules; the diff overlay runs only for a revision and is left out.

clusters.label: Route the import command
rules: Turns the command line into one `type:ImportRequest` for the freeze.
Reports the frozen generation and exits with code 0.

clusters.label: Check the output against the graph
rules: Binds the output to the exact graph bytes and to the flow lineage.
Any error rejects the whole output before a write.

clusters.label: Assign clusters and derive layers
rules: Code writes every step ID, membership, color, and digest.
A self-check recomputes every derived layer before a write.

clusters.label: Write the generation and pointer
rules: Writes the generation before the pointer, so a reader never sees a pointer to a missing file.

takes: The process arguments after the program name, and the locked standard input.
does: Passes both to `fn:run`.
returns: The exit code from `fn:run` becomes the process exit code.

takes: The arguments from `fn:main`. The first argument is `value:flow`.
does: Drops `value:flow` and calls the flow command runner.
`value:help` prints the usage. Any other command line indexes a codebase.
returns: Prints the one output document that comes back.

does: Detects `value:--json` before the parse, so an invalid command can also answer in JSON.
`fn:parse` builds an import action from the name, the graph, the input, the author options, and the store.
onFail: A missing or unknown option exits with code 2 and prints the usage.

does: Calls `fn:import` with the store, the JSON flag, the flow name, the graph file, the input path, the author options, and standard input.

steps.title: Resolve the author and read input

does: Turns the author flags into an agent `type:Author` with a name and a model ID. Without author flags the author is `value:system`.
`fn:ensure_flow_keys` resolves the semantic edges of the step keys before the import takes the store lock.
Reads the output bytes from the `value:--input` file, or from standard input for `value:-`.
returns: Passes an `type:ImportRequest` to `fn:import_flow`. The author comes from the command line, never from the agent output.

requires: A flow name that is a lowercase slug.
A valid graph file name and a valid author.
does: Calls, in order: `fn:parse_output`, `fn:lock_store`, `fn:read_merged_graph`, `fn:read_current`, `fn:prior_rules`, `fn:check_agent_flow`, `fn:build_intent`, `fn:freeze`, `fn:write_current`.
Holds the store lock until it returns. The next steps follow these calls as siblings.

requires: The bytes parse as `type:AgentFlowOutput`, tagged by `field:outcome`, with no unknown fields.
onFail: A syntax or shape error becomes one `value:invalid_output` issue.
A `value:no_flow` answer ends the import with exit code 1 and writes nothing.
returns: A `value:flow` answer goes back to `fn:import_flow`, which then takes the store lock with `fn:lock_store`.

requires: A valid name and no symbolic link.
Graph schema 1, valid node identities, and valid edge endpoints.
returns: The graph and the digest of the exact file bytes. `fn:read_merged_graph` adds the cached semantic edges, and `fn:import_flow` binds the flow to this name and digest.

does: Reads `file:flows/flow-generation/current.json`. The pointer is missing for a new name.
onFail: With a parent, a changed graph file or digest is a `value:stale_graph` error.
returns: No current generation, so `fn:prior_rules` gives the `value:initial` purpose with no prior step IDs.

takes: The `type:AgentFlow`, the `type:PriorContext`, and the graph keys.
requires: Each text in Unicode NFC, without outer whitespace, and within its length limit.
One to eight unique clusters that steps use, each with its input and output models and one to three rules.
A step ledger with at least one slot. Each mark has a known kind, and a function mark names a graph function.
Each `field:nodeKey` in the graph, and each `field:clusterKey` in this output.
The same cluster on all steps of one function.
onFail: With any error, `fn:import_flow` returns a rejection. The CLI prints every issue, exits with code 2, and writes nothing.

takes: The `type:CheckedFlow`, the graph, the binding, and the prior step IDs.
does: Collects the distinct node keys of the steps and asks `fn:fact_layer` for their facts.

takes: The referenced node keys and the graph.
does: Projects only the referenced nodes: key, name, kind, language, path, content hash, signature, and documentation.
Hashes each projection into a fact digest, and keeps only the edges between referenced nodes, sorted and without duplicates.

takes: The `type:FactLayer` from step 12. This is the same call, not new work.
does: `fn:step_id` gives each new step `value:st-` plus 16 hex characters of a digest of the flow ID, the node key, and a counter.
Each step records the fact digest of its node.
returns: The `type:IntentLayer`. A parent with equal intent and facts would return `value:kept` without a write. A new name has no parent.

does: Derives the code-owned layers in a fixed order: assignment, view, diff for a revision only, generation, digests, and then a self-check.
Starts with `fn:assign`.
Runs the `value:step-labels` rules assigner with the `value:agent_labels` policy and the unanimous membership rule.
Each step label becomes a step decision. Each function becomes one member of its cluster, with its visit count.
returns: The `type:AssignmentLayer`. Its input digest hashes exactly the labels that the assigner reads.

takes: The steps and the call edges of the `type:FactLayer`.
does: Classifies each step against the step before: flow start, same function, call, return to caller, sibling call, indirect call, return to ancestor, or no static edge.
Gives each cluster a `value:flow-bright/1` color and records the step runs of each cluster.
returns: The `type:ViewLayer`. A transition is a static relation, not a runtime observation.

takes: The layers, after `fn:freeze` sets the ordinal, the purpose, the parent digest, and the provenance.
does: Hashes the RFC 8785 canonical JSON of the facts, intent, assignment, and view layers.
returns: The `type:Digests`. The generation digest excludes the provenance, so the same output on the same graph always gives the same digest.

requires: `fn:verify_artifact` recomputes every derived layer and digest. `value:flow verify` runs the same check later.
onFail: Any error fails the import before a write.

does: Names the file `file:flows/flow-generation/generations/<ordinal>-<digest>.json`. An identical file stays. A different file is a conflict.
writes: The generation file first, then `file:current.json` with the generation digest and the ordinal.

takes: The target path and the bytes.
requires: No symbolic link at the target.
does: Writes a temporary file in the same folder, syncs it, and renames it over the target. A failure removes the temporary file.
writes: The generation file, and then the pointer, each atomically.

takes: The frozen outcome from `fn:import_flow`, which released the store lock.
returns: Prints the frozen generation, its purpose, its digest, and its file, and exits with code 0. The server builds the catalog when the viewer asks.
